title: Plaintext autokey at a long lag, 9-33 letters back or ahead, decided by chains through the unknown letters, on 666,993 keyword tableaux
k4_result: 48.0 billion settings (666,993 alphabets x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort x fed letter numbered in M/A-Z/KRYPTOS x sign x look-back/look-ahead x lag 9-33 x constant c). Lags 9-23 (7 to 15 exact checks each, every c): 0 settings pass all their checks; 0.79 chance passes were expected (0.26 each at lags 17, 18, 23, which have 7 checks). Lags 24-33 (0 to 5 checks): 5,374,898 settings passed their checks and the English gate and were decrypted as far as the clues force them (58-86 letters); the best reads -5.95 per quadgram on the big model over 40 quadgrams outside the clues (English needs -5.1, planted texts read -4.3 to -4.9), word coverage 0.57; none reaches -5.1. Nothing at lag 21 or 14, the lags the idea was about.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, each on a different third of the alphabets (222,331 each, one full pass together). Lags 9-23: 0 settings pass in each. Lags 24-33: 1,589,236 / 1,602,797 / 1,672,480 settings read in full (4.86 million together, K4 5.37 million); best readings -5.95, -6.04, -6.13 (K4 -5.95); none reaches -5.1.
planted: 6/6: lag 21 back (11 checks, read -3.99), lag 13 ahead (11 checks, -4.52), lag 17 back (7 checks, -4.41), lag 24 ahead (5 checks, -4.87), lag 28 back with c = 0 (no check, found as the best English reading, -4.67), lag 27 ahead with c = 11 (no check, best English reading, -4.28); each on its own tableau among 9,000 sampled alphabets. Separately the fast chain test and a slow plain implementation pass exactly the same settings on random ciphertexts, every survivor of the full run was re-checked with the slow one, and the English gate lost 0 of 300 planted low-lag messages.
scope_limits: Dictionary keyword alphabets only (plain, ~cols, ~keyed) plus A-Z and KRYPTOS; layouts M/M, M/AZ, AZ/M, M/KR, KR/M; fed letter times +1 or -1 plus one constant. Lags 27, 28 and 29 have no check at all: there every c = 0..25 was read on A-Z, KRYPTOS and the 220,318 plain keyword alphabets, but only c = 0 on the 446,675 transposition-mixed alphabets. Lags 24-33 rest on reading English, not on exact checks: a setting is dropped unless one of the two runs forced next to the clues (12 and 11 letters) looks English and the other is not hopeless (kept 99.9% of K1-K3 windows, 300 of 300 planted messages), so a plaintext that is not ordinary English there (numbers spelled oddly, a second cipher layer) would be missed. NOT covered: a repeating word on top of the autokey, hidden (non-dictionary) alphabets, multipliers other than +-1, clue blocks moved from their places, cipher-text feed (ideas 90 and 96 did that), transposition before or after. Controls saw a third of the alphabets each.

negative.family: Long-lag plaintext autokey (a row keyed by the row above)
negative.hypothesis: K4 is a plaintext autokey on a keyword tableau whose key letter is the plaintext letter 9 to 33 places back (rows of 21 or 14 keyed by the row above) or ahead.
negative.scope: Chains through the unknown letters: each clue letter fixes its class mod the lag, classes holding two clue letters give exact checks (15 at lag 9 down to 7 at lags 17, 18, 23; 11 at lags 13, 14, 20, 21). Lags 9-23: all checks required, every constant c. Lags 24-33 (0-5 checks): forced 58-86 letters read on the big English model; at lags 27-29 all c on 220,318 plain keyword alphabets, c = 0 on 446,675 transposition-mixed ones. 666,993 alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and two mixed forms) x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort x fed letter numbered in M/A-Z/KRYPTOS x added or subtracted x look-back/look-ahead; 48.0 billion settings.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 0 of 48.0 billion settings pass at lags 9-23 (0.79 expected by chance); at lags 24-33 the best of 5.37 million readings is -5.95 against -5.1 needed (controls: 3 shuffled K4s on a third of the alphabets each, 0 passes, best readings -5.95, -6.04, -6.13; planted 6/6). Not covered: a repeating word on top, hidden alphabets, c other than 0 at lags 27-29 on the mixed alphabets.

follow_ups: Long-lag plaintext autokey with a short repeating word on top (period 2-7): the chains still close, but each step adds an unknown word letter. At lags 9-14 (11-15 checks) a word of up to 4 leaves 7+ checks; solve the word letters from the first chains by the same table trick and require the rest. Planted: lag 14 with a word of 3.

The symmetric case found here (fed letter numbered like the plaintext, Vigenere +, Beaufort -) makes two-step chains independent of c, so with ONE hidden alphabet on all three sides a two-step chain reads x[C1] - x[C2] = x[P0] - x[Pn]: linear in the 26 unknown places with no constant. Lags 19-22 give 9-11 such equations; test with the linear solver of round 9 and demand distinct places.
